question: You unproject points near your camera's image edge with the datasheet focal length, and they are centimetres off. What is the fix?
options: Tune fx and cy by hand until the edge looks right
Re-read the datasheet focal length more carefully
Measure fx, fy, cx and cy from a known target
explanation: Nominal intrinsics differ from the real ones, so measure them.

question: You photograph a flat checkerboard once. What does this one view give you in this method?
options: One full 3D pose of the robot base
explanation: H = K [r1 r2 t] relates grid coordinates to pixels.

question: You move a checkerboard in front of your camera. Why must the views have different tilts?
options: Views that only shift repeat the same constraints
The solver needs a different board size for each view
A tilted board is easier to detect in the image
explanation: Identical orientations add no new equations on B.

question: Each checkerboard view you add contributes equations to B. How many does one view add?
options: Only one equation from each view
Six equations, one per entry of B

question: Your checkerboard corners have 1 px of noise. What happens to the linear result when you go from 3 to 10 views?
options: The error doubles, as each view adds noise
The error drops to nearly zero in practice
The error roughly halves but does not vanish
explanation: More constraints average the noise, but it does not vanish.

question: Your calibration returns cx far from the image centre and fx very different from fy. What is your first suspicion?
options: The values are normal for a wide-angle lens
Views too few or too alike, giving a weak fit
The sensor has failed and needs replacing
explanation: The linear solution amplifies noise when views are poor.
